subject: english
question:
Choose the correct meaning of the given idiom/phrase from the options:
"to be off base"

options.text: To be on the right track

solution:
The correct answer is: **3 i.e. To be wrong or mistaken**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"to be off base"** means to be incorrect, mistaken, or far from the truth. (गलत होना)
 
 
• **Example:** His assumptions about the project were completely off base; he misunderstood the requirements.
 
 
• **"To be wrong or mistaken"** perfectly aligns with the meaning of "to be off base." (गलत या भ्रमित होना)
 
 
• **Example:** If you think I’m going to support this decision, you’re completely off base!
 
 
• Hence, the correct meaning of "to be off base" is **"to be wrong or mistaken."**

Therefore, the correct answer is: **To be wrong or mistaken**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To be on the right track** (सही दिशा में होना): Refers to doing something correctly or heading in the correct direction.
 
 
• **Example:** The team is on the right track with their new marketing strategy.
 
 

 
• **To be confused** (उलझन में होना): Refers to being uncertain or puzzled about something.
 
 
• **Example:** I was confused by the instructions for assembling the furniture.
 
 

 
• **To change your mind** (अपना विचार बदलना): Refers to deciding to do something different from what was initially planned.
 
 
• **Example:** She decided to change her mind and accept the job offer.
